assumptions: client_ref is required in every tool request (section 2: 'pass it to every tool'). It is the brief's customer identifier, so in every tool body it is mapped to the engine's customer-identifier slot 'customer_id'.
Amounts: get_account and create_promise both use integer cents, so amount_scale is 100 and promise_scale is null. The brief gives no rounding rule, so promise_round is null.

Final band (31 to 60 days): the floor is overdue_cents, not the floor field for the product type. This is set with a band-level floor_field and a band ladder: the overdue amount on the week close, then the overdue amount (which is the floor) on the deadline. In this band, a 'too much' reply is told that the overdue amount is the lowest that can be recorded.

Proposal 1 is the overdue amount on the week close, or the floor if the customer already said the overdue amount is too much (full_or_floor). Proposal 2 (firm and final bands only) is the floor on the deadline. The soft band has 1 proposal; firm and final have 2. The opening ask 'Can you pay all of this in full today?' is not counted as a proposal, because rule 11 numbers the proposals after it. So opening_is_attempt is false.

'Too much' before any proposal: the floor is offered once, on the date on the table (today, before any proposal), and uses no proposal, so too_much_floor is 'asked_date'. The customer is told the rest stays overdue.

Week close: if today is the last business day of this week, use the last business day of next week (week_end_today = next_week). If the week close is after the account's deadline, the account's deadline is used instead.
Deadlines are the Nth business day after today, with today never counted, so they always fall on a business day. deadline_adjust stays at the default previous_business_day.

A refusal after a counter-offer is a flat refusal and does not bring back the value the customer named (refuse_deadline_is_refusal true). Any proposal with the same amount and date as one already refused on that account is skipped.

Callback: today or the next business day, 09:00 to 18:00, later than now. The brief does not say today must be a business day, so business_days_only is false. The brief does not say how many times to ask for a time, so the default max_asks of 2 is used.

Identity: the verify_identity response fields are passed (verified), identity_complete (all verified) and wrong_left (wrong answers left). The API has no hint field, so hints is empty. An unreadable answer comes back with ok=false and is not counted. The brief gives no postcode length, so length is omitted. Two refusals end the check as unverified / declined.
The optional comment field of add_note is not mapped.
Deceased customer: the brief gives no code. This uses no_contact / no_callback, the closest allowed no_contact cause.
The brief does not cover the meaning of 'next <weekday>', how many 'I don't want to talk' replies end the call (2), or asking 'anything else' after a promise. The defaults are used for all three.
The brief does not cover changing a promise that is already saved, so the agent says it cannot be changed on this call.
Opening: the brief requires saying the call is recorded. This is worded in active voice ('we record this call').

close_call: no_commitment uses the note code of the first account, in get_account order, whose note is not already_paid. settled is used only when every account is noted already_paid. promised is used if at least one promise was saved. handed_over is used after any transfer, even after a saved promise, and no notes are written on a transfer.
Rule 24: a failed create_promise is retried once. If it fails again, the account is noted system_issue and the remaining accounts carry on.
